governance.note: neiso-49 = the neiso-48 keeper recipe on current main (measured Algonquin/EIA-MA-citygate DAILY gas-hub basis overlay + dual-fuel oil re-attribution + EIA-930-pinned hydro budget with 2024 plant-capacity backfill + biomass/OTHER measured must-run + historic CAMPD outage overlay + dual-limb temperature-correlated reliability floor + floor-class outage exemption + post-solve ORDC scarcity-price overlay + tranche_startup_amortization + CC_REGULAR econ band 1.00->1.15, CT_PEAKER tmax limbs scrubbed) with TWO structural changes, both grounded in the repo's frozen derive methodologies and neither tuned to a residual. (1) Connecticut ST_GAS NET-LOAD reliability-commitment limb (reliability_floor_coeffs_NEISO.csv, derive_reliability_coeffs.py netload path): the rule-19 re-grounding of the two disabled, unidentified ST_GAS temperature limbs (tmax rho=0.23 < RHO_MIN; tmin n=8 < N_MIN). The NEISO legacy-steam fleet (Montville, ORIS 546) is committed by ISO-NE on TIGHT-SYSTEM days, cold AND hot (Feb-2023 arctic blast; the post-Mystic Jun-Aug 2024/2025 heat events; Jan+Dec 2025): daily peak net-load unifies the driver (median committed day = p93 of daily-peak net-load; Spearman rho 0.51, n=329 flagged days; commit_frac 0.2796 x physical min_stable 0.12 -> floor_pct 0.0336) — the CAISO-CT netload-limb precedent (rebuild-plan review decision 2). All-24h boiler gate, 48h steam event bridging, no temperature gate. Two derive-script correctness fixes shipped with it (offline CEMS days counted as offline rather than dropped — the single-plant commit_frac=1.0 saturation artifact; netload threshold percentile restricted to the 2023-2025 derivation span so the 2019-21 EIA-930 backfill and rule-22 holdout periods cannot enter). Rule-24 reconcile: when armed together with Component B (neiso_winter_fuel_mustrun, default off), Component B drops ST_GAS from its scope so the two floors never stack. (2) NEISO-MEASURED offer bands for the de-leaked-to-neutral classes (scripts/derive_campd_marginal_hr.py --iso NEISO -> data/raw/reference/neiso_campd_marginal_hr_summary.csv), closing the 'later disciplined-calibration item' the 0c6c833 de-leak ledgered (rule #1 second step — offer grounding on measured data, the attestation's own named C3a/C3b closure path): ST_GAS 0.79/0.85/0.89 (native measured marginal HR 0.642/0.692/0.731, a genuinely RISING measured ramp, x the NEISO-native CC reach ratio 1.223 = CC_REGULAR econ_high band 1.15 / native CC marginal 0.940 — the NYISO run-32 convention, no cross-ISO value, rule #26); CC_CHP 1.15/1.17/1.19 (native flat 0.94-0.97 x 1.223, thin monotone spread; n=5 units, wide IQR disclosed); CT_PEAKER econ bands stay neutral 1.0 — now AFFIRMED by measurement (native CT marginal is flat-to-FALLING, 0.808/0.745/0.700: the removed ERCOT 1.27->1.98 ramp had no NEISO basis; the real above-cost CT component is startup amortization, already priced); CT_CHP stays neutral (n=1 unit, unidentifiable). Effect: the committed steam unit is priced into merit for its daytime load-following (ST_GAS 2025 D-1 PASSES for the first time: profile_r 0.844, cv_ratio 2.87; 2023 off-peak CV collapse fixed: ratio 35.4 -> 4.6) and the commitment floor carries near-zero forced energy (D-2 ST_GAS forced share 0.0 all years — the floor is scaffolding, dispatch is economic). Disclosed honest costs (rule #1, NOT to be won back by a storage or offer tune): C5b 2025 deepens -49.3% -> -56.3% (0.91 vs 2.08 TWh) because the measured-cost steam tranche shaves the artificial evening peaks the PS fleet was arbitraging — the missing spread is the ledgered winter/scarcity price-formation gap; and 2023 ST_GAS profile_r reads 0.49 vs the keeper's 0.619 — the old value correlated a 13-hour spiky artifact, the new one is a real profile with a genuine mis-phase (model evening-peaked vs actual midday-peaked event days), the honest remaining gap. No adder/haircut/sigmoid tuned to a residual; the LP is not pinned to actuals.
governance.validation_note: Reproducible from the committed bundle: scripts/run_calibration_full.py --iso NEISO --year 2023 2024 2025 --commitment --reliability-floor --hydro-backfill-year 2024 --hydro-eia930-monthly --gas-hub-basis-daily --scarcity-price-overlay --tranche-startup-amortization --out-dir results/calibration/neiso_stgas_netload (the netload limb is registry-enabled; the measured offer bands are code defaults in _NEISO_OFFER_CURVE). Leave-one-year-out (rule #22): both changes are measured-grounded values (CAMPD marginal HR pooled 2023-2025; the netload limb fit pooled 2023-2025 like every reliability limb) — no value was fitted to a single year's residual; the D-1 delta is year-heterogeneous and reported per-year (2025 PASS, 2024 r 0.659->0.725 cv-artifact remains, 2023 r honest-lower). Zero-forcing ablation twin registered alongside (2026-07-06-neiso-49-stgas-netload-ablation, rule 21). REMAINING OPEN C7 GATE: ST_GAS 2023 profile_r 0.49 (mis-phased event profile) and 2024 cv_ratio 0.0 (flat-floor-only year: at $2.19 gas the unit clears no merit hours, so the committed profile carries no intra-day variation) — both ledgered below with their diagnosed root causes (engine-vs-derivation net-load basis mismatch flags 27/36/58 days vs the derivation's ~110/yr — a follow-up consistency item; sub-min-stable LP relaxation sliver — a commitment-integrality follow-up via class_commitment_overrides whose CAMPD-bin early-return currently blocks it; and the 2024 price-depression C3a family). NEISO overall determination remains NOT-YET on the caveat budget (hard C2+C7 2>1; soft C3a/C3b/C3c/C5b 4>2).

exceptions.metric: C2 gas family grid-delivered TWh (preliminary 2025 vintage)
exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (EIA-930 gas-vs-OTHER fold-in + preliminary-vintage incompleteness)
exceptions.reason: 2025 is a preliminary EIA-923 vintage — per-class actuals are incomplete (audit 2026-07-04: 13/30 prior CC_REGULAR plants missing, 57% reporting; gas family incomplete). The scorer falls back to the EIA-930 grid gas cell, which INCLUDES geothermal+biomass (~5.2 TWh); the correction formula under-corrects because the preliminary vintage's per-class cells are incomplete. Same categorization issue documented for the complete-vintage years, where the per-class C1 gate PASSES under the load-scaled band. When the full 2025 vintage reconciles, the per-class gate replaces this family fallback. NOT closable by adjusting model dispatch.

exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (winter fuel-inventory scarcity rent / reserve scarcity)
exceptions.reason: The energy-only LP caps the cold-hour price at the dual-fuel oil-parity (~$258/MWh). The post-solve ORDC scarcity overlay (ISO-NE-grounded LOLP curve: VOLL $2000 = Tariff III.1.10.1A offer cap, MCL 1200 MW ~ Millstone 3, sigma 900 MW = PAF Study 2022) fires and modifies econ_prices for capacity economics but does not change the persisted LP prices. The fast-start tranche pricing added in this run lifts the summer-evening and shoulder peak pricing but cannot produce >$300 cold-snap hours — that scarcity rent is the finite winter fuel INVENTORY the LP prices as an unlimited flow. Closable only via the documented winter fuel-inventory / seasonal-reliability build (docs/multi-iso/neiso-winter-fuel-inventory-plan-2026-07.md), NEVER via an offer adder tuned to the tail.

exceptions.magnitude: model 0.91 vs actual 2.08 TWh (-56.3%; was -49.3% on the neiso-48 keeper)
exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (downstream of the price_tail / winter-scarcity item)
exceptions.reason: PS arbitrage throughput tracks the intraday price spread. The fast-start tranche pricing + econ-band re-anchor recovered a third of the gap ENDOGENOUSLY (0.74 -> 1.05 TWh, no storage-formulation change — per the neiso-ps-undercycling diagnosis, the PS number may only move downstream of price structure). The residual under-cycle is winter-concentrated: the LP's cold-month spread stays compressed at the dual-fuel oil-parity cap, and the real Northfield fleet additionally cycles near-daily for reserves/regulation the energy-only LP does not remunerate. Closes with the winter fuel-inventory build and/or in-LP reserve co-optimization value reaching storage; never via a storage knob. DEEPENED by neiso-49 (honest cost, rule #1): the measured-cost ST_GAS committed tranche shaves the artificial evening peak the PS fleet was arbitraging; the residual spread is the same ledgered winter/scarcity price-formation gap, and per the neiso-ps-undercycling diagnosis it may only be recovered via price structure, never a storage knob.
